Since requestedSlug is also gated behind IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED, self-hosted installs now get neither slug nor requestedSlug, and billing-enabled installs set slug directly bypassing the requestedSlug flow. Verified directly in create.handler.ts diff.

judged_text: The boolean-spread-to-ternary rewrite inverted the slug condition: slug was previously written when !IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED, but is now written only when IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED is true. With team billing disabled (self-hosted installs) organizations are created with no slug and no requestedSlug, permanently breaking org slugs/URLs for every newly created org; with billing enabled, slug is now set directly alongside requestedSlug, bypassing the requestedSlug approval flow that isOrganizationVerified/isOrganizationConfigured metadata is meant to gate.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/organizations/create.handler.ts`, the conditional spreads were inverted. Previously `slug` was set only when `!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED` (`...(!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug })`) and `requestedSlug` was set only when `IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED` (`...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { requestedSlug: slug })`). The diff changes this to `...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {})` and `...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { requestedSlug: slug } : {})`, meaning when team billing is disabled, neither `slug` nor `requestedSlug` is written, and when enabled, both are written. This matches the finding’s claim of broken slug creation/approval-flow behavior based on the shown logic.
